newsitem.title: USA: Mexico, Colombia criticize drug certification.
newsitem.headline: Mexico, Colombia criticize drug certification.

text.p: Mexican and Colombian officials on Monday criticised the U.S. practice of certifying allies in the drug war and said Washington should concentrate on reducing demand for illegal narcotics within its own borders.

The United States announced on Friday that it had certified Mexico as an ally in the war on drugs but again denied certification to Colombia. Decertified nations can face aid cuts and economic sanctions.

Representatives of the two governments, speaking at a news conference during a U.S. Customs conference on international trade, said it was inappropriate for the United States to be certifying foreign nations as drug war allies.
"We reject that kind of policy," Luis Ortiz Monasterio, Mexico's consul-general in Miami, said.
"The Mexican government combats narco-traffic because it represents a threat to our country, not to get certified by the United States," he said.
Mexican authorities revealed on Friday that drug lord Humberto Garcia Abrego, brother of Mexico Gulf cartel chief Juan Garcia Abrego, had escaped from custody.
Garcia's escape was revealed several hours after Washington's announcement, though he had fled late Thursday or early Friday. The escape prompted talk in Washington of a move to decertify Mexico.
Ortiz said Mexico was doing "nothing" to avoid decertification. "This is an internal problem of the United States."

Felipe Jaramillo, Colombia's vice minister for foreign trade, said Colombians were disillusioned with the U.S. government but said his country appreciated that harsh sanctions had not yet been imposed.
Some Colombian officials have quietly expressed anger that Mexico, rocked by numerous drug corruption scandals, won certification while Colombia was denied.
Horacio Ayala, Colombia's director of taxes and customs, said developed countries had not put enough effort into fighting consumption.
"If the more industrialised countries had given the same effort as the less developed countries, the war would have been in a more advanced stage," he said.
